findings.evidence: Both sections state "The [people operations / benefits] office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" and "A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day" / "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time"
findings.fix: Consolidate this information in one location; remove the duplicate "Overview" section (lines 59-62).
findings.location: "Program Overview" section and "Overview" section (lines 5-7 and lines 61-62)
findings.violation: The same information about publishing the reimbursement log is presented twice in different sections, making the document redundant and confusing.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Move this content to a troubleshooting or known issues section, or remove it entirely if it is not part of the standard process.
findings.violation: This sentence describes an operational failure (backup reviewer not being informed) as if it were a normal step in the application process, creating confusion about standard procedures.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Clarify the manager's role: either state that the manager uses the standard checklist, or explain how discretion and the checklist work together.
findings.violation: This contradicts line 27 which states "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list," making it unclear whether the manager follows the checklist or uses discretion instead.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Revise to "The deposit offsets costs the employee has already paid."
findings.violation: The phrase "at this point in time" is redundant; the sentence is unnecessarily wordy.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Change to "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The benefits team may request a brief photo verification once annually."
findings.violation: The document uses formal third-person language throughout but switches to informal second-person pronouns ("you" and "we") in this sentence, creating tone inconsistency.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with "Additionally," or remove the transition word.
findings.violation: The transition word "Similarly" does not logically connect this statement to the previous sentence about equipment maintenance and photo checks.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal."
findings.fix: Revise to reduce repetition: "Employees record the approved equipment category (called the 'stipend item') on the request form. Finance reconciles it against the request log each month, and Payroll releases payment after monthly review."
findings.violation: The term "stipend item" is repeated five times in consecutive sentences, creating confusing and awkward repetition in a section meant to clarify terminology.

findings.evidence: Sections titled "Overview," "Program Coordination," and "Review Responsibility" repeat information already presented in the "Program Overview," "How to Apply," and "Approval Timeline" sections.
findings.fix: Remove duplicate sections and reorganize the document with a single clear structure: Program Overview, Eligibility, How to Apply, Approval Timeline, Required Documentation, Reimbursement Amounts, Restrictions and Exceptions, and Questions and Contact Info.
findings.violation: The document structure is disorganized with duplicate sections that confuse the order of information and make it unclear where to find specific guidance.
